full_judgment:
2. Heard the learned Advocate and perused the application. It appears that the plaintiffs filed Other Suit No.9 of 1993 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Anowara praying for declaration that they are entitled to get renewal of the lease of toll collection of the disputed road from 15.3.93 to 14.3.94 as per Clause 2 of the agreement with the defendant-opposite party and also for perpetual injunction. After filing the said suit petitioner prayed for temporary injunction and by order dated 20.3.93 an adinterim injunction up to 14.3.93 was granted. By subsequent order dated 15.3.93 the said order of adinterim injunction was extended up to 14.3.94. Defendant preferred Civil Revision No. 1246 of 1993 before this court against the said order and this Court issued Rule and stayed operation of the said order dated 15.3.93. Said Rule was made absolute granting temporary injunction for one month from the date of receipt of the order by the trial Court with direction to dispose of the suit immediately. By order dated 1.3.94 order of adinterim injunction was set aside by the Assistant Judge as one month already expired from the date of receipt of the order. Petitioner filed Miscellaneous Appeal No.86 of 1994 against the said order. By order dated 23.4.94 the said Miscellaneous Appeal was dismissed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong with cost of Taka 500.00. Against that order petitioner filed a Revisional application and this court issued Rule being Civil Revision No.1446 of 1994 on 2.5.94 but refused to grant adinterim injunction. Subsequently petitioner again moved this court with a fresh application for injunction which was also refused on contest by order dated 18.5.94. In the meantime Other Suit No. 9 of 1993 was transferred to the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Chittagong in pursuance of order dated 6.4.94 passed by the District Judge, Chittagong in transfer Misc. Case No. 108 of 1994 and the learned Subordinate Judge received the record of the case on that very date and fixed 12.4.94 for hearing after renumbering the suit as Other Suit No. 53 of 1994. On that date petitioner filed an application for an adjournment on the ground of illness of the wife of his Advocate and the case was adjourned to 16.4.94. On 16.4.94 defendant filed an application for dismissing the suit as the renewed period of lease expired on 14.3.94. After hearing that application by order dated 17.4.94 suit was fixed for peremptory hearing on 20.4.94. On that date on the ground of petitioner's Advocate's absence the case was adjourned to 30.4.94. On 30.4.94 petitioner again took adjournment with a certificate from Mr. A. Baset Majumder, learned Advocate that he will move this court for an order of stay and on that ground the learned Subordinate Judge adjourned the hearing of the suit to 6.5.94. Now the petitioner has moved this application under section 24(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure for transferring the suit within the jurisdiction of any District Judge other than the District Judge, Chittagong on the allegation that petitioner will not get the desired relief from any learned Court functioning under the supervisory jurisdiction of the learned District Judge Chittagong. It has been contended in ground No.1 that the learned Subordinate Judge, Chittagong fixed the suit for hearing on 16.5.94 without considering that this Court issued Rule on 2.5.94. 

 4. On query learned Advocate has disclosed that deponent Md. Nurul Amin son of Abdus Sattar at present of 14/13, Babar Road, Mohammadpur, Dhaka is a clerk of a learned Advocate of this Court But from the affidavit it appears that he has disclosed his profession as a businessman concealing the fact that he is an Advocate's clerk. It is not the function of an Advocate's clerk to swear affidavit in support of the application filed by a party posing as his tadbirkar. His function is to assist the Advocate under whom he works. But if he misleads the Court posing as tadbirkar of a party concealing his real identify as Advocate's clerk he is transgressing limits of his profession. Unless the learned Advocate under whom he is working controls his such activities transgressing limits of his profession he may eventually bring disrepute on the learned Advocate. Moreover, swearing affidavit in support of an application filed and moved before this Court is not a mere formality. Court is to act relying on such application supported by an affidavit. If it is found that an application is supported by an affidavit of a person who is not competent to swear affidavit Court has no option but to throw out such application like this application. It is the applicant, his agent or tadbirkar who is competent to swear affidavit in support of an application. Tadbirkar is a person who looks after the case in the Court on behalf of a party and is conversant with the facts and circumstances of a case. He is essentially a person different from the Advocate's clerk. This distinction should be borne in mind by a learned Advocate while an affidavit is being sworn by the deponent in support of an application. Otherwise the applicant will suffer.
